title: Wiz Research's AI-augmented reverse engineering of GitHub's closed-source git binaries, with Claude Code and IDA MCP, finds a critical push-option injection giving remote code execution on GitHub.com and GitHub Enterprise Server; GitHub reproduces it in 40 minutes, patches github.com by 7:00 pm UTC on 4 March 2026 and finds no exploitation
summary: Wiz's AI-aided reverse engineering found a critical GitHub RCE (CVE-2026–3854); github.com was patched the same day, no exploitation found.
account: On 4 March 2026 Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw to GitHub, later CVE-2026–3854. It sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) patches from 10 March, and found no exploitation.
purpose: Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool, built to read a codebase, edit files, run commands and connect to external tools over MCP. Wiz used it, with IDA MCP, to automate reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries. Analyzing code for flaws is within that general purpose. The benefit was an application of what the tool was built to do rather than a departure from it.
system: AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling used by Wiz Research: Claude Code (named by The Register and WebProNews) with IDA MCP for automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries (named by Wiz), applied to GitHub.com's backend and GitHub Enterprise Server 3.19.1
model_version: Not named in the cited sources. Wiz's write-up credits 'AI-augmented tooling, particularly automated reverse engineering using IDA MCP' and does not name Claude. The Register and WebProNews name Claude Code.
developer: Anthropic (Claude Code); the maker of IDA MCP is not named in the sources
deployer: Wiz Research (Sagi Tzadik, Nir Ohfeld, Ronen Shustin, Hillai Ben-Sasson, Yuval Avrahami, Noam Malron)
domain: Cybersecurity: vulnerability research and software supply chain
segment: Bug bounty research: AI-assisted reverse engineering of closed-source server binaries

ratings.reason: GitHub closed a critical remote code execution hole in its git push pipeline within hours of the report. The fix reached github.com at 7:00 pm UTC on 4 March 2026. GitHub also shipped patches for six GitHub Enterprise Server release lines. Wiz earned what GitHub calls one of the highest rewards in the history of its Bug Bounty program. The loss avoided is hypothetical. GitHub's forensic investigation found that no other account had triggered the code path. No customer data was accessed, modified or exfiltrated. The benefit is an exposure closed rather than a demonstrated loss prevented.

ai_role.statement: The AI's documented contribution is speed of analysis, on the researchers' own account. Wiz writes that AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling, particularly IDA MCP, let it rapidly analyze GitHub's compiled binaries and reconstruct internal protocols. Wiz says that speed would not have been feasible manually. Sagi Tzadik told Dark Reading that with AI tools it took under 48 hours from idea to working exploit. The Register adds that the team used Claude Code “to take a lot of the legwork out of the process”. The hypothesis, the exploit, the report and the fix were human work. Six named Wiz researchers confirmed RCE on GHES 3.19.1 and wrote what GitHub called a thorough report. GitHub's security and engineering teams reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed the fix. GitHub's own post, the CVE record and the GHES release notes describe a Bug Bounty report without mentioning AI. The AI-assistance claim therefore rests on Wiz and on outlets quoting Wiz. Wiz's write-up, in the text as read, names IDA MCP and not Claude.

evidence.title: Overview
evidence.quote: Claude Code is an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools.

produced_by: A closed-source target that researchers could obtain and disassemble. GitHub's backend git services also ship as GitHub Enterprise Server binaries. Those binaries gave automated reverse engineering something to work on, and GHES 3.19.1 gave a place to confirm the exploit.

AI-augmented tooling for reverse engineering: IDA MCP (per Wiz) driven by Claude Code (per The Register). It reconstructed internal protocols and traced where user input could influence server behavior across the pipeline.

Experienced vulnerability researchers: six named Wiz authors formed the hypothesis and built and confirmed a working exploit. They wrote what GitHub called a thorough report that clearly demonstrated the impact.
A beneficiary with a Bug Bounty intake and an on-call security team. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes of the report. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC the same day.
must_hold: AI output has to be confirmed by exploit, not trusted. Wiz confirmed RCE on a GHES 3.19.1 instance before reporting. That is why GitHub could validate the report in 40 minutes.

The receiving organization must be able to patch its own service and ship fixes to self-hosted customers. GHES customers stayed exposed until they upgraded to the patched versions released from 10 March 2026.
Disclosure must wait for the patches, here from 4 March to 28 April 2026. No exploitation had occurred, so the benefit is an exposure closed, not a loss recovered.

headline: Wiz finds a critical GitHub RCE with Claude Code and IDA MCP
metric: went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours

comparator.against: manual reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries without AI tooling
comparator.before: an impractical amount of time and manual effort (Wiz); months' worth of manual analysis, per The Register's account of Wiz
comparator.after: from idea to working exploit in less than 48 hours
comparator.quote: However, extracting and auditing the sheer volume of compiled blackbox binaries that run this pipeline historically required an impractical amount of time and manual effort. But this is Round 2, and the landscape has shifted. By leveraging AI-augmented tooling-particularly automated reverse engineering using IDA MCP-we were able to do what was previously too costly.

later.note: GitHub's 28 April 2026 disclosure confirmed the same-day fix, patches for all supported GitHub Enterprise Server releases, and a forensic investigation that found no exploitation beyond the researchers' own testing.
later.quote: In less than two hours we had validated the finding, deployed a fix to github.com, and begun a forensic investigation that concluded there was no exploitation.

fields.summary: Wiz's AI-aided reverse engineering found a critical GitHub RCE (CVE-2026–3854); github.com was patched the same day, no exploitation found.
fields.account: On 4 March 2026 Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw to GitHub, later CVE-2026–3854. It sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) patches from 10 March, and found no exploitation.

fields.account: On 4 March 2026 Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw to GitHub, later CVE-2026–3854. It sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) patches from 10 March, and found no exploitation.

produced_by: A closed-source target that researchers could obtain and disassemble. GitHub's backend git services also ship as GitHub Enterprise Server binaries. Those binaries gave automated reverse engineering something to work on, and GHES 3.19.1 gave a place to confirm the exploit.

AI-augmented tooling for reverse engineering: IDA MCP (per Wiz) driven by Claude Code (per The Register). It reconstructed internal protocols and traced where user input could influence server behavior across the pipeline.

Experienced vulnerability researchers: six named Wiz authors formed the hypothesis and built and confirmed a working exploit. They wrote what GitHub called a thorough report that clearly demonstrated the impact.
A beneficiary with a Bug Bounty intake and an on-call security team. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes of the report. It deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC the same day.
must_hold: AI output has to be confirmed by exploit, not trusted. Wiz confirmed RCE on a GHES 3.19.1 instance before reporting. That is why GitHub could validate the report in 40 minutes.

The receiving organization must be able to patch its own service and ship fixes to self-hosted customers. GHES customers stayed exposed until they upgraded to the patched versions released from 10 March 2026.
Disclosure must wait for the patches, here from 4 March to 28 April 2026. No exploitation had occurred, so the benefit is an exposure closed, not a loss recovered.

display.answer: Wiz researchers obtained GitHub’s compiled software that also shipped with Enterprise Server. They used AI tools to examine it and developed an exploit that they confirmed on version 3.19.1. Their report showed that remote code execution was possible. GitHub reproduced the issue within 40 minutes and fixed github.com that evening.
